about: A save never overwrites someone else's change (docs/APP-CAPABILITIES-PLAN.md, step 5). Every record of a versioned entity carries a version, a whole number in its own column; find reads it, a save of a stored record writes only when it is still the one read, and adds one. A save or a delete of a record someone changed since is refused with Clarity's savedSince and changes nothing; a save anyway writes regardless; reload reads the record as it is stored now. Undo compares the version instead of the whole row. A file source refuses a save when its file changed on disk since it was read. Each case is run on its own, on a fresh database: the table item (id, name, row_version) for the database cases, the CSV file below for the file case. Steps work on named copies of records: two copies of one record are what two windows hold. Every step expects ok unless it says otherwise; a refusal is the error with the key and English of refusal (or of undoRefusal for undo).

refusal.english: Someone else changed this record since you opened it. Reload it to see their change.

undoRefusal.english: This was changed since, so it cannot be taken back

table: CREATE TABLE item (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL, row_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1)

steps.insert: save a new record with this name as copy; it is stored with version 1
steps.read: copy is the record of copy of, found by its id
steps.set: sets the name of copy, in the copy only
steps.saveAnyway: saves copy regardless of its version
steps.reload: copy is read again as it is stored now
steps.stored: the stored record of copy has this name and version, or is gone
steps.stepSave: saves copy as one undo step (a handler run that changed it)
steps.undo: takes back the last undo step
steps.redo: does the last undone step again

cases.name: a new record starts at version 1, and each save adds one
the second of two copies is refused and changes nothing
a save anyway writes regardless, and adds one
reload reads the change, after which the save goes
a delete of a record changed since is refused; with the version read it goes
a save of a record deleted since is refused as not found
undo compares the version: a save since with the same values still refuses it
undo and redo add one each, so a copy read before them is refused

file.about: A file source: the file is the unit. A save is refused when the file changed on disk since it was read or last written (its size and modification time differ, and so do its bytes); the same bytes written again are no change. Every step is a save of the first record with the name given.

stepsHelp.save: sets the name of the record read first and saves it
stepsHelp.rewrite: writes the file's own bytes to it again (its modification time changes, its bytes do not)
stepsHelp.write: another program writes this text to the file
